sources.title: Dimasa Language: Structure and Texts
sources.linguistic_info: Definitive contemporary grammar of the Haflong dialect of Dimasa; covers phoneme inventory (17 consonants, 5 vowels), morphosyntax, 8 case markers, verbal suffix slots, tense-aspect neutralization under negation, and discourse texts.

sources.title: An Outline Grammar and Dictionary of the Kachari (Dimasa) Language
sources.publisher: Eastern Bengal and Assam Secretariat Press
sources.linguistic_info: Early structural description, grammatical paradigms, comprehensive English-Dimasa and Dimasa-English vocabulary, numerals, and conversational phrases.

sources.title: Dimasa Word Book: A Classified Vocabulary
sources.linguistic_info: Comprehensive classified semantic lexicon of Dimasa words spanning flora, fauna, tools, kinship, food, anatomy, actions, and numerals.

sources.title: A Descriptive Analysis of Dimasa
sources.linguistic_info: Detailed descriptive phonology and morphology of Dimasa; confirms 17 consonant inventory and analyses nominal compounding and verbal affixation.

sources.title: Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. III: Tibeto-Burman Family, Part II (Bodo, Naga, and Kachin Groups)
sources.publisher: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing
sources.linguistic_info: Classification of Dimasa under the Bodo group, comparative vocabulary, grammatical outline, and translated specimen texts.

sources.title: The Tibeto-Burman Languages of Northeastern India
sources.series: The Sino-Tibetan Languages (Graham Thurgood & Randy J. LaPolla, eds.)
sources.linguistic_info: Comparative analysis of the Bodo-Garo (Sal) subfamily, phonological developments, and morphological characteristics of Dimasa.

sources.title: Dimasa Kachari: History, Society and Clans
sources.linguistic_info: Historical records of the 40 Sengphong (male clans) and 42 Julu (female clans), traditional village governance, and customary laws.

sources.title: Dimasha Society and Their Folk Songs
sources.linguistic_info: Detailed documentation of Dimasa folk songs (Murithaih, Rjabkharmin), musical instruments (Khram, Muri), and wedding and funeral traditions.

sources.title: The Traditional Systems of the Dimasa
sources.linguistic_info: Detailed documentation of Bushu Dima celebrations, Daikho deity system, priestly offices (Zonthra, Hojai), and traditional attire (Rigu, Rikhaosa).

sources.title: Dimasa Grao Thairili & Orthographic Guidelines
sources.linguistic_info: Standard Roman orthography, phoneme-grapheme correspondences, and standardized spellings approved for school education and literature.

sources.title: Bodo and Dimasa Heritage Digital Archive
authors: Tezpur University Centre for Endangered Languages
sources.linguistic_info: Open digital corpora of Dimasa audio recordings, glossed folktales, proverbs, children's games, and oral history.
